Rung 2 — Flow Model Placement

LoRA on 8 consecutive SparseTransformer blocks (rank=4, 163,840 params) in the 25-step flow model. Placement varies: early (blocks 0–7), mid (blocks 8–15), late (blocks 16–23).

📍 slat_flow_model · cross-attention · to_q + to_kv · 8 blocks (early=0–7 / mid=8–15 / late=16–23) · rank=4 · 163,840 params
Model: Flow model — 25-step Euler denoiser (SLaT generation stage)
Before (frozen)
q   = W_q  · x_feats       # sparse features, dim=1024
kv  = W_kv · x_ctx         # DINOv2 conditioning tokens
out = softmax(q·kᵀ/√d) · v
y   = W_out · out
After (+ LoRA)
q   = W_q  · x_feats + B_q  A_q  · x_feats   # A∈ℝ^{r×1024}, B∈ℝ^{1024×r}
kv  = W_kv · x_ctx   + B_kv A_kv · x_ctx     # A∈ℝ^{r×1024}, B∈ℝ^{2048×r}
out = softmax(q·kᵀ/√d) · v                   # W_out, W_fc frozen
y   = W_out · out
Takeaway: Adapts only the conditioning pathway (to_q gets SLaT features, to_kv gets DINOv2 image tokens). Result: late placement (blocks 16–23) wins at 17.4 dB.

Rung 3 — Decoder 1/3 Placement (budget-matched)

LoRA on 4 consecutive SparseTransformer blocks in the 12-block SLaT mesh decoder. Budget-matched to rung2 (~200k params).

📍 slat_flow_model · cross-attention + MLP · ALL 5 layers (to_q + to_kv + to_out + fc1 + fc2) · 8 blocks · rank=4 · ~200k params
Model: Flow model — 25-step Euler denoiser (SLaT generation stage)
Before (frozen)
q   = W_q  · x_feats
kv  = W_kv · x_ctx
z   = softmax(q·kᵀ/√d) · v
out = W_out · z
h   = gelu(W_fc1 · x)      # MLP, 1024→4096
y   = W_fc2 · h            # MLP, 4096→1024
After (+ LoRA)
q   = W_q  · x  + B_q   A_q   · x
kv  = W_kv · c  + B_kv  A_kv  · c
out = W_out · z + B_out  A_out · z
h   = gelu(W_fc1 · x + B_fc1 A_fc1 · x)
y   = W_fc2 · h  + B_fc2 A_fc2 · h
# Budget-matched to rung 2 (~200k params)
Takeaway: Does more layers-per-block beat more blocks? No — rung 2 late (17.4 dB, 2 layers) beats rung 3 late (15.7 dB, 5 layers) at matched budget. Block count > layer depth in the flow.

Rung 5 — Decoder Scaling Ladder

Progressive scaling within the decoder: from output head only → last block → 1/3 of blocks (placement sweep) → all 12 blocks.

📍 slat_decoder_mesh · self-attention + MLP · to_qkv + to_out + fc1 + fc2 · blocks: 5.1=head / 5.2=b11 / 5.3=4 blocks / 5.4=all 12 · dim=768
Model: SLaT decoder — mesh generator (SLaT → FlexiCubes appearance stage)
Before (frozen)
qkv = W_qkv · x_feats      # self-attn, dim 768→2304
out = W_out · z
h   = gelu(W_fc1 · x)      # MLP, 768→3072
y   = W_fc2 · h            # MLP, 3072→768
After (+ LoRA)
qkv = W_qkv · x + B_qkv A_qkv · x   # A∈ℝ^{r×768}, B∈ℝ^{2304×r}
out = W_out · z + B_out A_out · z
h   = gelu(W_fc1 · x + B_fc1 A_fc1 · x)
y   = W_fc2 · h  + B_fc2 A_fc2 · h
# Injected via forward hooks; flow model runs completely frozen
Takeaway: Key insight: LoRA in the DECODER (not the flow). The flow runs frozen — same SLaT for all rungs. LoRA adapts how the decoder writes appearance to the FlexiCubes voxelgrid. 5.4 (all 12 blocks) hits 22.95 dB — +3.6 dB over the best flow-model result.

v4 — LoRA on out_layer

The fix strategy that was TBD above. Every stage before out_layer mixes information across voxels — windowed self-attention in the 12 transformer blocks, and convolution in the two SparseSubdivideBlock3d upsamplers. out_layer is a per-voxel linear map with nothing downstream that mixes, so an edit placed there cannot propagate.

📍 slat_decoder_mesh · out_layer · 96 → 101 channels · delta added to [53:101] only · rank=4
Confirmed visually. v1 (inside attention) leaves a pale patch on the handle. v3 (MLP-only, attention untouched) washes the handle and rim white — proving the upsamplers alone carry the corruption. v4 shows no handle artifact at any epoch.

GT | frozen | v1 | v3 | v4 — frame 075 @ epoch 30

The white cast — and why it was the loss, not the adapter

v4 removed the handle artifact but desaturated the whole object. Cause: TRELLIS's generated teapot and the video's teapot are different shapes — silhouette IoU 0.76. 16% of the rendered teapot sits on white background in the GT, so the loss instructs those pixels to become white. That thin rim supplies 56% of the total colour gradient, sign [+,+,+] on every channel. The adapter reads voxel features, not position, so it cannot obey that only at the rim — it learns "be whiter" globally.

📍 fix: loss region (render ∪ GT) → (render ∩ GT) · gradient scale held at v4's normaliser · one variable changed
Predicted in advance, then measured. Modelling the adapter as a global additive shift, least squares over each region predicts the outcome. Against v4's actual output across all 150 frames: union error 0.027±0.014, intersection error 0.111±0.019 — union closer on 149/150 frames, paired t = 40.0. v4 did exactly what the union region demanded.

CONFIRMED. ΔB fell 0.238 → 0.105, past the 0.16 decision threshold set before the run. ΔG landed at 0.086 against a prediction of 0.085. Gradient clipping never engaged (clip_frac 0.0000), so the comparison against v4 remained a genuine one-variable ablation. Held PSNR reads 8.49 vs v4's 10.66 — expected, since that metric is scored on v4's union region, which includes the rim we deliberately stopped supervising; intersection PSNR is 13.04.

360° turntable — the texture does not paste

First multi-view render of any adapter in this project. Every previous turntable was the 12-block decoder LoRA (run 31e5b3e8), not v4.

📍 60 azimuths · elevation 15° · frame 075 fixed · frozen | v4
Two findings. First, v4's edit is applied uniformly at every angle — it is not a decal correct from the front and wrong elsewhere, so the suspected texture-pasting failure is not present. Second, and less comfortable: the frozen baseline already produces correctly wrapped lava all the way around, and v4 degrades it from every viewpoint. Before rung8, the adapter was worse than doing nothing.

0° / 90° / 180° / 270° — frozen | v4

Does the frozen decoder give time-varying geometry?

Geometry channels [0:53] are decoded from the per-frame SLaT, so in principle the frozen decoder already outputs a mesh that changes shape every frame with no adapter involved. Measured directly: chamfer distance and multi-view silhouette against frame 1, alongside the GT video's own silhouette change.

📍 frozen decode · 150 frames · chamfer subsampled to 20k verts · silhouette at 0/90/180/270°
Shape change, frame 1 → 150Silhouette areaArea spreadMin IoU vs f1
GT video+5.43%5.27%0.948
TRELLIS frozen mesh+0.30%0.33%0.991
Tracking ratio0.063chamfer signal is 365× the numerical noise floor — the movement is real, just tiny
The backbone will not give deformation for free. TRELLIS captures 6% of the video's shape change. The right-hand panel is the sharper statement: chamfer rises to 0.005 by frame 20 and then goes completely flat — the mesh makes one small adjustment early and freezes for the remaining 130 frames, while the GT deforms monotonically throughout. A geometry adapter writing deform[8:32] is therefore justified by measurement rather than assumption.

Silhouette area · multi-view drift · 3D surface motion

Where this leaves the pipeline. The contamination question is closed — out_layer is the only position where a per-voxel edit provably stays local, and the v1/v3/v4 comparison is the evidence. The white cast is closed — it was a supervision artifact from a silhouette mismatch, and restricting the loss region fixes it. Geometry is open: the frozen backbone supplies almost none of the deformation the target video contains, so extending the adapter to the geometry channels is the next step, with the silhouette term restored to the loss since a mismatched rim becomes signal rather than noise once shape is trainable.
